rules.heading: Naming Consistency
rules.shipped:
### Naming Consistency
Follow established naming patterns for variables, functions, classes, and files throughout the project.

rules.heading: Automatic Formatting
rules.shipped:
### Automatic Formatting
Use automated tools to enforce consistent indentation, spacing, and line breaks.

rules.heading: Descriptive Names
rules.shipped:
### Descriptive Names
Choose names that clearly communicate intent; avoid cryptic abbreviations or single-letter identifiers outside tight loops.

rules.heading: Focused Functions
rules.shipped:
### Focused Functions
Write functions that do one thing well; smaller functions are easier to read, test, and maintain.

rules.heading: Uniform Indentation
rules.shipped:
### Uniform Indentation
Standardize on spaces or tabs and enforce with editor/linter settings.

rules.heading: No Dead Code
rules.shipped:
### No Dead Code
Remove unused imports, commented-out blocks, and orphaned functions instead of leaving them behind.

rules.heading: No Backward Compatibility Unless Required
rules.shipped:
### No Backward Compatibility Unless Required
Avoid extra code paths for backward compatibility unless explicitly needed.

rules.heading: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)
rules.shipped:
### DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)
Extract repeated logic into reusable functions or modules.

rules.heading: Let Code Speak
rules.shipped:
### Let Code Speak
Write code that explains itself through structure and naming.

rules.heading: Comment Sparingly
rules.shipped:
### Comment Sparingly
Add brief comments only when the logic isn't self-evident from the code.

rules.heading: No Change Comments
rules.shipped:
### No Change Comments
Avoid comments about recent fixes or changes; comments should be timeless explanations, not changelogs.

rules.heading: Predictable Structure
rules.shipped:
### Predictable Structure
Organize files and directories in a logical, navigable layout.

rules.heading: Up-to-Date Documentation
rules.shipped:
### Up-to-Date Documentation
Keep README files current with setup steps, architecture overview, and contribution guidelines.

rules.heading: Clean Version Control
rules.shipped:
### Clean Version Control
Write clear commit messages, use feature branches, and add meaningful descriptions to pull requests.

rules.heading: Environment Variables
rules.shipped:
### Environment Variables
Store configuration in environment variables; never commit secrets or API keys.

rules.heading: Minimal Dependencies
rules.shipped:
### Minimal Dependencies
Keep dependencies lean and up-to-date; document why major ones are included.

rules.heading: Consistent Reviews
rules.shipped:
### Consistent Reviews
Follow a defined code review process with clear expectations for reviewers and authors.

rules.heading: Testing Standards
rules.shipped:
### Testing Standards
Define required test coverage (unit, integration, etc.) before merging.

rules.heading: Feature Flags
rules.shipped:
### Feature Flags
Use flags for incomplete features instead of long-lived branches.

rules.heading: Changelog Updates
rules.shipped:
### Changelog Updates
Maintain a changelog or release notes for significant changes.

rules.heading: Build What's Needed
rules.shipped:
### Build What's Needed
Avoid speculative code and "just in case" additions (see minimal-implementation.md).

rules.heading: Clear User Messages
rules.shipped:
### Clear User Messages
Show helpful, actionable messages without exposing internal details or security-sensitive information.

rules.heading: Fail Fast
rules.shipped:
### Fail Fast
Validate inputs and check preconditions early; reject invalid data before it causes deeper issues.

rules.heading: Typed Exceptions
rules.shipped:
### Typed Exceptions
Use specific exception types instead of generic ones to enable precise error handling.

rules.heading: Centralized Handling
rules.shipped:
### Centralized Handling
Catch and process errors at appropriate boundaries (controllers, API layers) rather than scattering try-catch throughout.

rules.heading: Graceful Degradation
rules.shipped:
### Graceful Degradation
When non-critical services fail, continue operating with reduced functionality rather than crashing entirely.

rules.heading: Retry with Backoff
rules.shipped:
### Retry with Backoff
Use exponential backoff for transient failures when calling external services.

rules.heading: Resource Cleanup
rules.shipped:
### Resource Cleanup
Always release resources (file handles, connections) in finally blocks or equivalent cleanup mechanisms.

rules.heading: Build What You Need
rules.shipped:
### Build What You Need
Create only methods, classes, and functions that will actually be called.

rules.heading: Clear Purpose
rules.shipped:
### Clear Purpose
Every method should either be called or improve code readability; nothing else.

rules.heading: Delete Exploration Artifacts
rules.shipped:
### Delete Exploration Artifacts
Remove helper methods and utilities created during development that ended up unused.

rules.heading: No Future Stubs
rules.shipped:
### No Future Stubs
Avoid empty methods, placeholder functions, or interfaces "for future extensibility".

rules.heading: No Speculative Abstractions
rules.shipped:
### No Speculative Abstractions
Skip factories, strategies, or adapters unless there's an immediate need.

rules.heading: Review Before Commit
rules.shipped:
### Review Before Commit
Verify all new methods have callers or serve a clear readability purpose before completing a task.

rules.heading: Unused Code Is Debt
rules.shipped:
### Unused Code Is Debt
Remove dead code promptly; it confuses readers and adds maintenance burden.

rules.heading: Server-Side Always
rules.shipped:
### Server-Side Always
Validate on the server; client-side validation alone is insufficient for security and data integrity.

rules.heading: Client-Side for Feedback
rules.shipped:
### Client-Side for Feedback
Use client-side validation for immediate user feedback, but duplicate checks server-side.

rules.heading: Validate Early
rules.shipped:
### Validate Early
Check inputs as early as possible and reject invalid data before processing.

rules.heading: Specific Errors
rules.shipped:
### Specific Errors
Provide clear, field-specific messages that help users correct their input.

rules.heading: Allowlists Over Blocklists
rules.shipped:
### Allowlists Over Blocklists
Define what's allowed rather than trying to block everything else.

rules.heading: Type and Format Checks
rules.shipped:
### Type and Format Checks
Validate data types, formats, ranges, and required fields systematically.

rules.heading: Input Sanitization
rules.shipped:
### Input Sanitization
Sanitize user input to prevent injection attacks (SQL, XSS, command injection).

home.heading: Prevent Injection Where Data Is Used

rules.heading: Business Rules
rules.shipped:
### Business Rules
Validate business logic (sufficient balance, valid dates) at the appropriate layer.

rules.heading: Consistent Enforcement
rules.shipped:
### Consistent Enforcement
Apply validation uniformly across all entry points (forms, APIs, background jobs).

rules.heading: Semantic HTML
rules.shipped:
### Semantic HTML
Use appropriate elements (nav, main, button) that convey meaning to assistive technologies.

rules.heading: Keyboard Navigation
rules.shipped:
### Keyboard Navigation
Make all interactive elements accessible via keyboard with visible focus indicators.

rules.heading: Color Contrast
rules.shipped:
### Color Contrast
Maintain 4.5:1 contrast for normal text; don't rely solely on color to convey information.

rules.heading: Alt Text and Labels
rules.shipped:
### Alt Text and Labels
Provide descriptive alt text for images and labels for form inputs.

rules.heading: Screen Reader Testing
rules.shipped:
### Screen Reader Testing
Verify all views work with screen readers.

rules.heading: ARIA When Needed
rules.shipped:
### ARIA When Needed
Use ARIA attributes to enhance complex components when semantic HTML isn't enough.

rules.heading: Heading Structure
rules.shipped:
### Heading Structure
Use heading levels (h1-h6) in proper order for clear document outline.

rules.heading: Focus Management
rules.shipped:
### Focus Management
Manage focus appropriately in dynamic content, modals, and SPAs.

rules.heading: Single Responsibility
rules.shipped:
### Single Responsibility
Each component should do one thing well.

rules.heading: Reusability
rules.shipped:
### Reusability
Design components to work across different contexts with configurable props.

rules.heading: Composability
rules.shipped:
### Composability
Build complex UIs by combining smaller components rather than creating monoliths.

rules.heading: Clear Interface
rules.shipped:
### Clear Interface
Define explicit, documented props with sensible defaults.

rules.heading: Encapsulation
rules.shipped:
### Encapsulation
Keep implementation details private; expose only what's necessary.

rules.heading: Consistent Naming
rules.shipped:
### Consistent Naming
Use descriptive names that indicate purpose and follow team conventions.

rules.heading: Local State
rules.shipped:
### Local State
Keep state as close to where it's used as possible; lift only when needed.

rules.heading: Minimal Props
rules.shipped:
### Minimal Props
If a component needs many props, consider composition or splitting it.

rules.heading: Documentation
rules.shipped:
### Documentation
Document usage, props, and examples to help team adoption.

rules.heading: Consistent Methodology
rules.shipped:
### Consistent Methodology
Stick to the project's chosen approach (Tailwind, BEM, CSS modules, etc.) across the entire codebase.

home.heading: Style the Way the Project Does

rules.heading: Work With the Framework
rules.shipped:
### Work With the Framework
Use framework patterns as intended rather than fighting them with excessive overrides.

home.heading: Style the Way the Project Does

rules.heading: Design Tokens
rules.shipped:
### Design Tokens
Establish and document consistent values for colors, spacing, and typography.

rules.heading: Minimize Custom CSS
rules.shipped:
### Minimize Custom CSS
Prefer framework utilities to reduce custom styling maintenance.

rules.heading: Production Optimization
rules.shipped:
### Production Optimization
Use CSS purging or tree-shaking to remove unused styles.

rules.heading: Mobile-First
rules.shipped:
### Mobile-First
Start with mobile layout and progressively enhance for larger screens.

rules.heading: Standard Breakpoints
rules.shipped:
### Standard Breakpoints
Use consistent breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop) across the application.

rules.heading: Fluid Layouts
rules.shipped:
### Fluid Layouts
Use percentage-based widths and flexible containers that adapt to screen size.

rules.heading: Relative Units
rules.shipped:
### Relative Units
Prefer rem/em over fixed pixels for better scalability.

rules.heading: Cross-Device Testing
rules.shipped:
### Cross-Device Testing
Test across multiple screen sizes to ensure a balanced experience.

rules.heading: Touch-Friendly
rules.shipped:
### Touch-Friendly
Size tap targets appropriately (minimum 44x44px) for mobile users.

rules.heading: Mobile Performance
rules.shipped:
### Mobile Performance
Optimize images and assets for mobile network conditions.

rules.heading: Readable Typography
rules.shipped:
### Readable Typography
Maintain readable font sizes across all breakpoints.

rules.heading: Content Priority
rules.shipped:
### Content Priority
Show the most important content first on smaller screens.

rules.heading: RESTful Principles
rules.shipped:
### RESTful Principles
Use resource-based URLs with appropriate HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE).

rules.heading: Consistent Naming
rules.shipped:
### Consistent Naming
Use lowercase, hyphenated or underscored names consistently across endpoints.

rules.heading: Versioning
rules.shipped:
### Versioning
Implement versioning (URL path or headers) to manage breaking changes.

rules.heading: Plural Nouns
rules.shipped:
### Plural Nouns
Use plural nouns for resources (`/users`, `/products`).

rules.heading: Limited Nesting
rules.shipped:
### Limited Nesting
Keep URL nesting to 2-3 levels maximum for readability.

rules.heading: Query Parameters
rules.shipped:
### Query Parameters
Use query parameters for filtering, sorting, and pagination.

rules.heading: Proper Status Codes
rules.shipped:
### Proper Status Codes
Return appropriate HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 404, 500).

rules.heading: Rate Limit Headers
rules.shipped:
### Rate Limit Headers
Include rate limit information in response headers.

rules.heading: Reversible
rules.shipped:
### Reversible
Always implement rollback methods for safe migration reversals.

rules.heading: Small and Focused
rules.shipped:
### Small and Focused
Keep each migration to a single logical change.

rules.heading: Zero-Downtime Awareness
rules.shipped:
### Zero-Downtime Awareness
Consider deployment order and backward compatibility for high-availability systems.

rules.heading: Separate Schema and Data
rules.shipped:
### Separate Schema and Data
Keep schema changes separate from data migrations for safer rollbacks.

rules.heading: Careful Indexing
rules.shipped:
### Careful Indexing
Create indexes on large tables carefully, using concurrent options when available.

rules.heading: Descriptive Names
rules.shipped:
### Descriptive Names
Use names that indicate what the migration does.

home.heading: Create Migrations with the Project's Tool

rules.heading: Version Control
rules.shipped:
### Version Control
Commit migrations; never modify existing ones after deployment.

rules.heading: Clear Naming
rules.shipped:
### Clear Naming
Use singular names for models and plural for tables (or follow framework conventions).

rules.heading: Timestamps
rules.shipped:
### Timestamps
Include created and updated timestamps for auditing and debugging.

rules.heading: Database Constraints
rules.shipped:
### Database Constraints
Enforce data rules at the database level (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, foreign keys).

rules.heading: Appropriate Types
rules.shipped:
### Appropriate Types
Choose data types that match purpose and size requirements.

rules.heading: Index Foreign Keys
rules.shipped:
### Index Foreign Keys
Index foreign key columns and frequently queried fields.

home.heading: Index What New Queries Filter On

rules.heading: Multi-Layer Validation
rules.shipped:
### Multi-Layer Validation
Validate at both model and database levels for defense in depth.

rules.heading: Clear Relationships
rules.shipped:
### Clear Relationships
Define relationships with appropriate cascade behaviors and naming.

rules.heading: Practical Normalization
rules.shipped:
### Practical Normalization
Balance normalization with query performance needs.

rules.heading: Parameterized Queries
rules.shipped:
### Parameterized Queries
Always use parameterized queries or ORM methods; never interpolate user input into SQL.

home.heading: Prevent Injection Where Data Is Used

rules.heading: Avoid N+1
rules.shipped:
### Avoid N+1
Use eager loading or joins to fetch related data in one query.

rules.heading: Select Only Needed Columns
rules.shipped:
### Select Only Needed Columns
Request only the columns you need rather than SELECT *.

rules.heading: Index Strategic Columns
rules.shipped:
### Index Strategic Columns
Index columns used in WHERE, JOIN, and ORDER BY clauses.

home.heading: Index What New Queries Filter On

rules.heading: Transactions
rules.shipped:
### Transactions
Wrap related operations in transactions to maintain consistency.

rules.heading: Query Timeouts
rules.shipped:
### Query Timeouts
Set timeouts to prevent runaway queries from impacting performance.

rules.heading: Cache Expensive Queries
rules.shipped:
### Cache Expensive Queries
Cache results of complex or frequent queries when appropriate.

rules.heading: Test Behavior
rules.shipped:
### Test Behavior
Focus on what code does, not how it does it, to allow safe refactoring.

rules.heading: Clear Names
rules.shipped:
### Clear Names
Use descriptive names explaining what's tested and expected (`shouldReturnErrorWhenUserNotFound`).

rules.heading: Mock External Dependencies
rules.shipped:
### Mock External Dependencies
Isolate tests by mocking databases, APIs, and external services.

rules.heading: Fast Execution
rules.shipped:
### Fast Execution
Keep unit tests fast (milliseconds) so developers run them frequently.

rules.heading: Risk-Based Testing
rules.shipped:
### Risk-Based Testing
Prioritize testing based on business criticality and likelihood of bugs.

rules.heading: Balance Coverage and Velocity
rules.shipped:
### Balance Coverage and Velocity
Adjust test coverage based on project needs and team workflow.

rules.heading: Critical Path Focus
rules.shipped:
### Critical Path Focus
Ensure core user workflows and critical business logic are well-tested.

rules.heading: Appropriate Depth
rules.shipped:
### Appropriate Depth
Match edge case testing to the risk profile of the code.
